CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 59-year-old male who presents with an upper respiratory infection that began approximately one week ago after outdoor yard work and landscaping. He reports feeling tired and experiencing shortness of breath. He denies wearing masks at the end of the summer and believes he caught a cold that has since worsened. Shortness of breath occurred primarily with exertion, such as lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil, causing him to become winded. He denies productive cough at this time but anticipates developing one. He reports feeling warm but attributed this to exertion rather than fever. He also endorses bilateral elbow pain and bilateral knee discomfort, which he relates to the physical labor involved in landscaping. He has received both COVID vaccines.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies seasonal allergies. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Endorses fatigue, exertional dyspnea, bilateral elbow pain, and bilateral knee pain. Otherwise negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (to be increased to 1000 mg twice daily)
Lisinopril 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed

SOCIAL HISTORY
Performs yard work and landscaping. Participates in barre classes for relaxation with his wife. Monitors blood sugar levels and blood pressure during work weeks but inconsistently on weekends. Diet generally good with occasional indulgences at social gatherings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Within normal limits, afebrile
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, sounds strong
Lungs: Scattered rhonchi bilaterally that clear with cough
Extremities: Mild edema of lower extremities noted
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral elbow tenderness to palpation

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia
Hemoglobin A1c: 8.0% (elevated)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/viral syndrome: Likely viral etiology. COVID test to be sent for confirmation. Expect resolution within a couple of days. Prescribed Robitussin for cough and advised ibuprofen or acetaminophen for fever management as needed.

2. Depression: Currently managing well with barre classes. Patient declines medication initiation or psychotherapy referral at this time. Will reassess in several months.

3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Hemoglobin A1c suboptimal at 8.0%. Increased metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin A1c in four months.

4. Hypertension: Currently well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Refill issued. Lipid panel ordered.

Follow-up appointment in four months. Patient instructed to contact office if symptoms worsen.
